key_insight: Strong water-wave turbulence shifts from weak-turbulence theory to breaking-dominated spectra earlier than expected because short-wave breaking is nonlocally controlled by the largest crest-scale waves.
engineering_relevance: For ocean, coastal, and wave-energy models, this means spectral energy transfer and breakup should not be assumed universal; forcing conditions can change the observed high-wavenumber and frequency spectra.
method: Reviews the history of gravity-wave cascade theory from Zakharov weak turbulence to Phillips and Kuznetsov breaking-wave spectra.
Argues that the frequency spectrum shape from breaking waves should persist across the cascade, while the wavenumber spectrum magnitude depends on pumping.
Uses a nonlocal interaction argument: shorter-wave breaking is governed by the amplitude of the longest waves riding beneath them.
evidence_signal: The paper is a theory-and-interpretation piece based on spectral arguments and literature comparison rather than new experimental or numerical data in the abstract.
watch_item: The strong-turbulence spectrum magnitude may be non-universal and sensitive to forcing details, so model calibration should not assume a single fixed high-wavenumber slope amplitude.
paper_title: On the spectra of strong turbulence on water surfaces
